title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 281 (Submission of report by Company Liquidator)

content.overview: Where the Tribunal has made a winding-up order or appointed a Company Liquidator, the liquidator shall, within sixty days from the order, submit to the Tribunal a report containing particulars of the nature and details of assets, debts, capital, causes of failure, and whether further inquiry is desirable, together with such other information as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Company Liquidator must file a detailed report to the Tribunal within 60 days of the winding-up order or appointment.
content.study: Section 281 requires the Company Liquidator, within sixty days of the winding-up order or of appointment, to submit a report to the Tribunal covering assets, debts, capital structure, causes of failure, viability steps, and whether further inquiry is desirable. The report is the foundation for Tribunal directions under section 282. Creditors and contributories may inspect it.

sections.heading: Time limit
sections.body: Report within sixty days of the winding-up order or of the liquidator's appointment.

sections.heading: Contents
sections.body: Nature and details of assets (including location and value), debts due, capital structure, causes of failure, steps for maximising value, and whether further inquiry is desirable.

sections.heading: Inspection
sections.body: A person claiming to be a creditor or contributory may inspect the report and take copies or extracts on payment of the prescribed fee.

provisions.title: Submission of report by Company Liquidator

examples.title: Sixty-day report
examples.body: After a winding-up order the Company Liquidator must file the section 281 report within sixty days; delay without extension risks directions under section 282.

examples.title: Inspection by creditor
examples.body: A creditor may inspect the liquidator's report filed under s. 281 and take extracts on payment of the prescribed fee.

hypotheticals.question: Must the liquidator's report under s. 281 be filed within a fixed period?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The Company Liquidator must submit the report to the Tribunal within sixty days from the winding-up order or from appointment.

misconceptions.trap: The liquidator's report can be filed at any convenient time.
misconceptions.correction: Section 281 fixes a sixty-day period from the order or appointment.
